subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: copying what a friend buys [Pitfall]
passage: In Class Six, Payal's new gel pen was the talk of the bench: gold clip, smooth ink, ninety rupees. Rishi looked at his own plain pen and felt small. That afternoon he spent nearly all his month's pocket money on the same pen. "Same as yours!" he said. Payal smiled politely. But the pen was heavy and smudged under his left hand, and by the third day his fingers ached. He caught himself sneaking his old pen out of his bag. Sarita Ma'am noticed and asked why. "I wanted it because Payal had it," Rishi mumbled, "not because I liked it."

qa.q: How much did the gel pen cost?
What was Rishi feeling when he looked at his own plain pen?
qa.a: Small and left out, wanting to fit in with the bench.

qa.q: What could Rishi do before buying next time, and why?
qa.a: He could try the item first and ask himself what he needs, so the choice is his own and not a copy.

qa.q: How might Sarita Ma'am see Rishi's answer?
qa.a: Sarita Ma'am probably sees an honest child who has spotted his own reason, and can be gentle about it.

grounding: A child buys the same expensive pen as a friend just to fit in, and later finds he does not like it.
